en.title: Minimum Operations to Convert Array
en.description: You are given a permutation of 1..n. Operation 1 rotates the array left by one position, and operation 2 swaps any two elements; once operation 2 has been performed, operation 1 can no longer be used. Find the minimum number of operations to turn the array into [1,2,...,n].
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n integers arr[i] forming the permutation. This site's judging constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 3000; arr is a permutation of 1..n. The original problem gives no numeric constraint on n; this range is the runtime bound this site set for the O(n²) reference algorithm.
en.output: Output a single integer, the minimum number of operations.
en.explanation: Enumerate k left rotations. The mapping from positions after rotation to target positions forms a permutation; if it has c cycles, the minimum number of arbitrary swaps is n-c. So the total number of operations is k+n-c; take the minimum over all k.
hints: For a fixed number of left rotations, the minimum number of arbitrary swaps equals n minus the number of cycles in the permutation.
All left rotations must happen before the first swap.
